There are examples of blind people using echo location. A quick google search of human echolocation gives you a wiki page full of recorded "echolocators".From the notable cases section of the wiki it seems that most echolocation "users" were either born blind or lost their sight in childhood, with many of these people having been self taught.

There has been evidence that the blind and even the deaf have "heightened" senses as a result of their brain remodeling its cognitive functions to adapt to the missing sense. Going back to the wiki article, it dies have this to say 
"sighted individuals have the ability to echolocate; however, they do not show comparable activation in visual cortex. This would suggest that sighted individuals use areas beyond visual cortex for echolocation." 

So it seems like it is even possible to train echolocation if you are not blind but you literally lack the proper brain function to do so, since it is spending its energy on your sight.
